query: How can peripheral physiology be modeled to allow cross‑loadings on affective pull (A_t) and control/resistance (C_t) in a hierarchical measurement model?

response.query: How can peripheral physiology be modeled to allow cross‑loadings on affective pull (A_t) and control/resistance (C_t) in a hierarchical measurement model?
response.answer: Peripheral physiology can be modeled using hierarchical measurement models with cross-loadings on affective pull and control/resistance by employing latent variable approaches that allow for shared variance between constructs. This method captures complex interactions between physiological responses and psychological factors.

results.content: Role of the gut-brain axis and gut microbiota in human metabolism ACADEMISCH PROEFSCHRIFT ter verkrijging van de graad van doctor aan de Universiteit van Amsterdam op gezag van de Rector Magnificus prof. 10 Chapter 1 AIMS The overall aim of this thesis is to shed more light on the role of the gut-brain axis in human glucose and lipid metabolism by linking the gut microbiota via its metabolites to the brain. Part II delves deeper into the role of the intestinal microbiota in the pathophysiology of metabolic disorders, on the one hand focusing on the role of novel metabolites in human insulin resistance, on the other hand thus aiming to answer the question whether a gut-brain axis exists in human metabolism. In chapter 3 we further elaborate on the role of the gut microbiota and its metabolites in the regulation of metabolism and satiety and the development of human obesity and TDM2, concluding with possible interventions that modulate intestinal entero-endocrine cells action.
